headline: The Bulls year peaks from the opener to December, and spring belongs to the Last Dance.
summary: Six-title nostalgia (1991-93, 1996-98) drives the Bulls year, with a rebuild on top. Interest peaks from the October opener through the Cup and December gifting, slides through winter and spikes again for the lottery, draft and Summer League. With no opening-night or Christmas Day game, Chicago has to build its own tentpoles: the Cup Nights and the spring Jordan and Last Dance anniversaries.

insights.title: Legacy sells when the team doesn't
insights.detail: Red-and-black Jordan-era product moves with Chicago and tourist traffic whatever the standings. The 31-51 finish with no playoffs didn't change that. Local fans split between the heritage buyer (1990s throwbacks, Jordan 23 and 45) and the current-roster buyer (Buzelis, Giddey, Wilson).
insights.implication: Run two tracks all year. Keep heritage graphics steady every month. Time a rookie and new-core capsule to the October opener and the holiday window.

insights.title: October is the peak, and the story is a new regime
insights.detail: It's Splitter's first season, with a new front office under EVP Bryson Graham. Add Powell, Claxton and rookies Wilson and Swain, and it's the first real change of direction in years. Bulls at Nuggets on ESPN on Oct 11 is the national preseason window. The league opens Oct 20 without a Bulls game on the opening-night slate.
insights.implication: New apparel can't land by the opener. Push existing Wilson, Buzelis and Giddey product and Association and Icon pieces before the home opener. Use the season to wear-test and seed 2027-28 launches.

insights.title: The NBA Cup is Chicago's November tentpole
insights.detail: The Bulls sit in East Group C with Boston, Atlanta, Charlotte and Washington. Cup Nights fall on Fridays from Oct 30 to Nov 27, plus Nov 24-25. Those Fridays compete with high-school football, bars and Thanksgiving-week travel. They are still the only guaranteed branded nights before December.
insights.implication: Throw Cup Night watch parties on Fridays and sell gifts from existing product. There is no Cup-specific colorway this year. Treat any Cup knockout games as a bonus, not the plan.

insights.title: No Christmas Day game moves gifting earlier
insights.detail: Chicago has no Christmas Day or opening-night national showcase. Holiday jersey and hoodie demand rides Black Friday, the Christkindlmarket, Magnificent Mile season and December games at the United Center.
insights.implication: Stage gift-ready packs, youth sizes and tourist-friendly Bulls and Chicago-skyline product from mid-November through Dec 20.

insights.title: Winter is quiet, spring brings the legacy back
insights.detail: January and February bring the end of Bears season, deep cold and a team out of contention. March adds St. Patrick's Day and the river-dyeing weekend. April through June bring Last Dance and Jordan nostalgia, plus the lottery and draft.
insights.implication: Use the Feb 11 deadline and the All-Star window for low-cost graphic tees. Hold premium drops for the lottery and draft months.

insights.title: Summer is a draft-hype and nostalgia market, not a game market
insights.detail: The May lottery, June draft and July Summer League carry the engagement. Caleb Wilson was First Team All-Summer League. In August, Cubs and Sox baseball, Lollapalooza and the Bud Billiken Parade own the conversation.
insights.implication: Pair rookie jerseys and draft-night product with city-festival drops, not team-only creative. In August, stay dormant on game-specific Bulls product.

vocabulary.meaning: Local shorthand for the team, tied to the Chicago accent and the 1990s identity.
The nickname began at Chicago Stadium (the dynasty-era home through 1994) and carried over to the United Center on Madison Street.
The 1997-98 title run and the 2020 documentary that revived Jordan-era demand.
Size, length, athleticism, physicality: the new front office's stated roster-building philosophy.
The cutting wind off Lake Michigan. Locals say it, unlike the tourist-coded Windy City.

designCues.cue: Bulls red as the dominant team color
designCues.use: Anchor for the team-specific capsule and the Association and Icon variants.
Accent for a city-first capsule that stands apart from the red-black team palette. Check Chicago flag usage rules before using the flag directly.

designCues.source: The Chicago flag's red six-point stars
designCues.use: A subtle repeat pattern on trim, sleeves or tonal graphics, not a literal flag.

designCues.source: Chicago winters and the January-February low in engagement
designCues.use: Heavier fleece, lined jackets and warm-up layers for the cold stretch, when fans still buy for function.
Throwback typography on tees. Confirm league and Jordan Brand licensing.
Everyday and off-court layering pieces for the long regular season.

productHooks: Player product for Wilson, Buzelis and Giddey, made from existing pieces around the Bulls home opener and the Cup Nights. A new capsule is a 2027-28 build.
Holiday gift pack for the Loop and Mag Mile season, with youth sizes and red-and-black warm-ups.
Spring heritage drop from March through June, built on the Last Dance era (licensing cleared) and draft-night product.
Winter-weight Chicago city layer in flag blue and red stars for the January-February cold stretch.
watchouts: Jordan-era imagery and Jordan's name need Jordan Brand and league licensing. Don't lift images without clearance.
Don't overstate a title run. The Bulls were 31-51 last season and power rankings rate them low. Lean on heritage and the new core, not contention.
Engage Bud Billiken and other South Side community events through local partners. Credit and pay the creators.
The Chicago flag is a municipal symbol. Check the rules before using it as a literal graphic.

keyDates.name: Bulls at Nuggets (ESPN preseason)
keyDates.why: A nationally televised preseason game and the first look at the Splitter-era roster.

keyDates.name: NBA opening night (no Bulls game)
keyDates.why: The league tips off with a tripleheader that excludes Chicago. The Bulls' own opener falls outside it.

keyDates.name: Emirates NBA Cup group play opens
keyDates.why: Cup Nights run Fridays through Nov 27. The Bulls are in East Group C with Boston, Atlanta, Charlotte and Washington.

keyDates.name: Cup group play ends
keyDates.why: The last group Friday falls on the day after Thanksgiving, which is also a heavy retail day.

keyDates.name: Cup quarterfinals
keyDates.why: Matters only if the Bulls win East Group C or take the best second-place spot.

keyDates.name: Cup championship at Hinkle Fieldhouse
keyDates.why: The Cup final moves to Butler's Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis, in the Bulls' Midwest backyard.

keyDates.name: Christmas Day slate (no Bulls game)
keyDates.why: Five games on ESPN/ABC without Chicago, so holiday gift demand falls before the day.

keyDates.name: MLK Day games
keyDates.why: A quadrupleheader on NBC/Peacock. The Bulls are not in the confirmed games.

keyDates.name: Trade deadline
keyDates.why: Moves involving Powell, Claxton or others could reshape player-specific demand.

keyDates.name: NBA All-Star Weekend, Phoenix
keyDates.why: A mid-winter product and content window.

keyDates.name: Regular season ends
keyDates.why: Opens the Play-In window of Apr 13-16 and the playoff-gear decision.

keyDates.why: A citywide event that overlaps with preseason, and a chance to reach run culture.
